summary.one_liner: ZeroClaw is a self-hosted personal AI agent runtime, shipped as a single Rust binary, that connects LLM providers to many chat channels and tools.
summary.what_it_does: ZeroClaw is configured through one TOML file (~/.zeroclaw/config.toml) and run locally with your own provider keys and workspace. It connects to LLM providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, and Ollama, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with fallback chains and routing when a provider fails. It receives messages from channels including Discord, Telegram, Matrix, email, voice, webhooks, and CLI, all handled by one agent loop. Tools include shell, browser, HTTP, hardware access, and custom MCP servers. It also provides an HTTP/WebSocket gateway with a web dashboard, an event-triggered SOP engine (MQTT, webhook, cron, peripheral), and ACP for editor integration over JSON-RPC stdio.
use_cases: run a personal AI assistant on my own machine
chat with an LLM agent through Discord or Telegram
automate shell and browser tasks with an agent
control GPIO, I2C, or SPI hardware from an AI agent
trigger agent workflows from webhooks, MQTT, or cron
connect an AI agent to my code editor
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | sh  (Unix installer; the URL was stripped from the README)
zeroclaw agent -a  (interactive chat using an agents entry)
notable: Single Rust binary with 30+ channel adapters and roughly 20+ model providers
Default 'supervised' autonomy: medium-risk actions need approval, high-risk blocked
Cryptographic tool receipts recorded for every action
Hardware support via a Peripheral trait for Raspberry Pi, STM32, Arduino, and ESP32
Event-driven SOP engine with approval gates and resumable runs
caveats: Default security mode requires approval for medium-risk actions; YOLO mode skips safety gates and is intended only for trusted dev environments
Some setup steps (Codex auth import, Claude setup token, docs submodule) add configuration work
Windows path uses a PowerShell prebuilt install rather than the Unix installer
keywords: run ai on my own machine
